svg.title: Ultrasonic distance instrument: block diagram
svg.desc: A Raspberry Pi Pico W reads two HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensors (Trig and Echo on GP20/GP21 and GP18/GP19, both sensors on 3.3 V) and a push button on GP17. It drives an RGB LED by PWM on GP12 to GP14, a 5 V relay module on GP16 and an SH1106 OLED display on I2C0 (GP4, GP5). Over its Wi-Fi it uploads the event log to ThingSpeak and gets the time from an NTP server. USB supplies 5 V; the relay uses VBUS 5 V, the sensors and the OLED the Pico 3V3 output. Five asyncio tasks run at fixed periods: button 20 ms, ranging 60 ms, indicator 50 ms, display 200 ms, cloud logger 20 s.
svg.text: BPC-DE2 · Raspberry Pi Pico W · MicroPython 1.29.0 · asyncio
RP2040 · plugged into the DFRobot Gravity board
Tasks (asyncio) and how often they run
Echo edges: hardware interrupt, time-stamped in µs
Each sensor is measured every 120 ms
LED and relay tick 1–5× per second, faster when closer
Clock set by NTP after connecting, then every 6 h
Pins, wire by wire: see the wiring diagram
